title: Fine-grained retention policy authoring with on-demand evidentiary bundle generation for prompts & telemetry
creator: Aisha Thompson
description:
Problem: Customers need an intuitive way to author retention rules that can express session-level, route-level, and artifact-type-specific TTLs for prompts, responses, request logs, and metrics while also producing legally defensible evidence bundles on demand. Current controls are coarse-grained (per-tenant or per-route TTLs) and do not support fast forensic exports or legal-hold overrides without heavy engineering.

This ticket proposes a product-native retention policy authoring surface that: (1) lets PMs/infra and tenant admins define hierarchical rules (global -> tenant -> route -> session) with overrides, (2) supports sampled and deterministic retention for metrics/logs, (3) provides a one-click on-demand evidence bundle generator that produces hashed, signed manifests and export archives, and (4) exposes an audit trail and export throttling for operational safety.
background: Regulators and enterprise security teams frequently request short-lived storage of PII or sensitive prompt outputs while maintaining the ability to produce legally admissible evidence bundles during audits or litigation. Engineering has added per-route TTLs and basic export endpoints, but exports are slow, lack manifest-level attestations, and cannot be scoped to session windows. We need a single UX + API that addresses authoring, previewing impact, and producing forensic artifacts without manual engineering work for each request from customers.
goals: Authoring UI to create hierarchical retention rules with inheritance and explicit overrides
Preview engine showing estimated storage and retention windows per tenant/route/sample
Deterministic sampler for high-volume telemetry to satisfy both legal forensics and cost constraints
On-demand evidence bundle builder that emits signed manifests, per-artifact hashes, and a time-bounded archive for auditor delivery
API endpoints for programmatic policy management and export orchestration
Operational controls: export throttling, retention-change audit log, and legal-hold toggle
non_goals: This ticket does not change the underlying physical archival storage format
This ticket will not implement multi-region synchronized retention enforcement (separate initiative)
This ticket will not replace enterprise SLA negotiation for Dedicated customers
proposal: We will deliver a combined Console and Admin API feature set: (A) Retention Policy Editor: a hierarchical policy model (Global -> Tenant -> Route -> Session) with typed rules for artifact_class {prompt,response,request_log,metric} and options for TTL, sample_rate (for metrics/logs), and legal_hold_exemptions. (B) Preview & Estimate: a dry-run simulation that projects retained volume over selected windows using historical traffic profiles. (C) Evidence Bundle Builder: a backend job that, given a time window or session ID list, collects artifacts, computes SHA-256 hashes, signs a manifest with KMS-backed keys, and packages the archive with metadata and an audit trail. (D) Audit / Operations: retention change history, export job queue with priority controls, and per-tenant quotas. We will provide Console flows and Admin API endpoints with RBAC integrations to restrict exports to authorized roles.
user_stories: As a tenant admin, I want to define a 30-day TTL for chat prompts by default but 180 days for routes tagged 'billing', so I can comply with billing dispute requirements.
As a security engineer, I want to mark a session as under legal hold so data within that session is excluded from TTL expiration until the hold is released.
As a compliance officer, I want to generate an evidence bundle for sessions between two timestamps and receive a signed manifest I can present to auditors.
As an infra operator, I want export jobs to be rate-limited and visible in a queue so exports do not overwhelm storage or cross-region bandwidth
acceptance_criteria: Retention Policy Editor: UI allows creating hierarchical rules with at least these fields: scope, artifact_class, ttl_days, sample_rate, legal_hold_flag, and a human-readable description
Preview Engine: Given historical sample data, the console shows estimated retained bytes and percent reduction for a selected policy within 1 minute of policy edit
API: Admin API endpoints exist for CRUD of policies and for triggering evidence exports; endpoints return structured job IDs and status
Evidence Bundle: Export job produces a ZIP with artifacts, a manifest.json containing SHA-256 per-file, and a KMS-signed manifest signature; artifact list must match requested scope
Security: Export endpoints enforce RBAC and require export role; KMS keys used must be configurable per-tenant
Operational: Export jobs surface metrics (duration, bytes, files) to Console and support manual retry on failure
design_notes: Console will reuse existing policy UI primitives but add a hierarchical view and conflict resolution UX (show effective TTL and source rule)
Evidence manifests follow a small v1 schema: version, generated_at, scope, artifact_count, file_hashes[], signer_key_id
Manifest signing to use existing KMS integration; include public key fingerprint in manifest for external verification
Sampler for metrics should be deterministic by hashing route + minute + tenant to a 0..1 range so exports are reproducible
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Beta): Expose policy editor and preview for internal tenants + a disabled evidence-generator for manual testing
Phase 2 (Gradual): Enable exports for partner tenants behind a feature flag with export throttling and monitoring
Phase 3 (General): Public GA with documentation, SDK examples, and a retention-policy-migration tool
risks: Large export jobs may saturate cross-region bandwidth or storage IO if not throttled
Incorrect sampling logic could lead to non-reproducible forensic evidence
Misconfigured policies could inadvertently increase retention costs for customers
test_plan: Unit tests for policy evaluation and inheritance rules
Integration test generating exports for synthetic traffic and verifying manifest hashes and signature validation
Load test for preview engine using 30 days of anonymized traffic to validate performance SLA
End-to-end QA with a partner tenant to validate legal-hold behavior
monitoring: Average export job duration and bytes processed
Policy-change event audit trail and anomalies (sudden TTL increases)
Sampling variance checks to detect drift in deterministic sampler
